rationale: Both independently caught the same genuine latent bug (pure-diffusion mode sets serving_tokenization=None, so the unguarded base(raw_request).create_error_response() call would raise on NoneType) and flagged the same test-coverage gap where base() is mocked. X is more calibrated: it centralizes the fix at the helper rather than nine call sites, explicitly labels the sibling-rename audit as an unverified 'lead, not a claim,' and reasons about CI failures using version-pin evidence (npu on v0.23.0 vs amd/intel on v0.24.0) rather than blanket alarm. Y restates the same core finding three times under different line anchors (inflating the finding count without new information), labels the three failing CI lanes a 'major merge blocker' despite the PR already being merged with only an lgtm approval, and its nit-level suggestion to re-add a state.openai_serving_tokenization compat alias undercuts the PR's own stated purpose. Ground truth carries no substantive reviewer concerns, so recall is near-ceiling and not discriminating for either.
